That the said Committee, upon Examination of several Witnesses, do find the same to be as followeth;

That great Numbers of Journeymen Taylors, in and about the Cities of London and Westminster, have of late, in order to procure themselves greater Wages than they used to have, combined together, and entered into Articles, competing one another to insist upon unreasonable 6 Wages,

7 Geo. I*

Wages, and to work fewer Hours in the Day than usually they used to do; and very often, when there is a Hurry of Work, insist upon Seven or Eight Shillings a Day: That, Complaint having been made thereof to his Majesty’s Justices of the Peace, several of the Journeymen Taylors have been bound over to the Quarter Sessions of the Peace; and Informations are ordered to be brought against them next Term; yet they continue their unlawful Meetings, and obstinate Behaviour, to the great Impoverishment of themselves, and Families; and may bring a great Burthen on the Publick:

That, by reason of these unwarrantable Proceedings, the Trade in general will be very much prejudiced; and will set bad Examples to other Artificers and Labourers. The Committee came to the following Resolution; Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That the Petitioners have fully proved the Allegations of their said Petition.

Raw Silk A Petition of several Persons, whose Names are there-used for unto subscribed, in behalf of themselves, and many Buttons,&c. Thousands of Men, Women, and Children, concerned in the Throwing, Twisting Dyeing, Manufacturing, and Making, of Needle-wrought Buttons, inhabiting in the Cities of London and Westminster, and Suburbs thereof, was presented to the House, and read; setting forth, That by an Act of Parliament, in the Fourth Year of the Reign of his present Majesty, intituled, An Act for making more effectual an Act, made in the Eighth Year of the late Queen Anne, intituled, An Act for employing the Manufacturers, by encouraging the Consumption of raw Silk, and Mohair Yarn, it is amongst other Things enacted, That no Person or Persons whatsoever shall make, set on, use, or bind, or shall cause to be made, sold, set on, used, or bound, upon any Cloth or wearing Garments whatsoever, any Buttons, or Button-holes, made of, or used, or bound, with Cloth, Serge, Drugget, Frize, Camblet, or any other Stuffs, that Cloths for wearing Garments are usually made of, upon Forfeiture of the Penalties therein provided: That, notwithstanding the said Acts, the Making of Buttons and Button-holes upon Men’s Apparel with all the said Materials, is become very general in almost all Places, if not in every Part of this Kingdom; and in Cities, and great Towns, in a manner universal: That the said Acts cannot be put in Execution, by reason of the Difficulties that do attend both the detecting and prosecuting the Offenders, who have contrived to evade the Force of the sai'd Act, in order to accomplish an undue Gain to themselves, and to the utter Ruin of Thousands of Families: And praying Relief.

That the Committee have endeavoured, with continued Application, to discharge the Trust reposed in them; At the Entrance into their Inquiry, they observed, the Matters referred to them were of great Variety , and Extent; many Persons were intrusted with different Parts in the Execution of this Law; and, under colour thereof* acted in an unwarrantable manner, in disposing of the Properties of many Thousands off Persons, amounting to many Millions of Money. In the Progress of their Inquiry, your Committee found it attended with many Difficulties: In some of the Books produced before them, false and fictitious Entries were made; in others, Entries with Blanks; in others, Entries with It as u res and Alterations, and in others, Leaves were tom out: They found further, that some Books had been destroyed, and others taken away, or secreted: Nevertheless your Committee are enabled to lay some Matters of Importance before the House, for their present Consideration.

The First Matter that offered itself to the Consideration of your Committee, was a Scene of Iniquity and Corruption; the Discovery of which, your Committee conceived to be of the highest, Importance to the Honour of Parliaments and the Security of his Majesty’s Government:

Your Committee observed, in the Account laid besom this House by the then Court of Directors of the South Sea Company, pursuant to your Order of the Twelfth Day of December last. That the Company were therein supposed to have received the Sum of One Million Two hundred fifty-nine thousand Three hundred Twenty-five Pounds, upon Account of Stock sold, to the Amount of Five hundred seventy-four thousand Five hundred Pounds Stock: Whereupon your Committee ordered the Company’s Cash Books to be laid before them; and, upon Inspection thereof, they found, at Fol. 120. and 121. tho several Entries of Stock, as sold for the Company, annexed at the End of this Report, N° I. $ the Total of which Entries amount to the said Sums of Five hundred seventy-four thousand Five hundred Pounds in Stock, and of One Million Two hundred fifty-nine thousand Three hundred Twenty-five Pounds in Cash: But it is very ob^ servable, that from the Article of the 4th of Febnuny 1719,. unto that of the 12° of April 1720, both inclusive, 5 Q there

South Sfea Company.

4 ^6 '

‘there is no mention madfe of the Name of any Person whatsoever, to whom the Stock is supposed to be sold:

The whole Accounts comprehended in these Two Pages of the Cash-book, and- entered in this concealed manner, appear, nevertheless, to have been stated and balanced by the Company’s Committee of Treasury, without expressing the Day when such Accolints were stated, and are subscribed by Sir John Fetlowcs, then Sub Governor; Mr. Charles Joy, then Deputy Governor; Sir Lambei't Blackwell, Sir Robert Chapl'm, Sir Theodore Janssen, Mr. Jacob Sawbi'idge, and Mr. Stephen Child, then Directors; all of them of the said Committee; and Sir Robert Chaplin, Sir Theodore Janssen, and Mr. Saw-bridge; at that time Members of this House.

Your Committee, upon this Occasion, take the Liberty to remind the House of a remarkable Period in the last Session of Parliament; That, upon the 2d of Febi'uary 1719, the House agreed to the Report of the Committee of the whole House, appointed to consider of that Part of his Majesty’s Speech, which related to the publick Debts, That the Proposals made by the South Sea Company should be accepted; and ordered a Bill to be brought in, pursuant to the said Resolution; which Bill, having passed this House, and afterwards the House of Peers, had the Royal Assent uyonThursday the 7th of April 1720.

Your Committee, surprised to see so large*an Account of Stock disposed of by the Company before the passing the Bill to enable the Company to increase their Capital Stock, and Fund; and before any Subscription, or Redemption, could be made, w'hereby their Capital Stock was increased; proceeded to examine carefully into that Transaction:

And, upon Examination of the late Sub and Deputy Governors, and the late Directors, of the-Sow^A Sea Company; Mr. Robert Knight, theii Cashier; Mr Robert Surman, then Deputy Cashier; Mr. John Grigsby, then Accountant; Mr. Charles Lochycr, then Second Account^ ant; and Mr. Matthexo JVymondesold, Broker, it manifestly appeared to your Committee, That the Company, at that time, was not possessed of such a Quantity of Stock, whereof they could then make an actual Sale, and Transfer; the Company having at that time, in their own Right, only a small Quantity of Stock not exceeding Twenty-five thousand Pounds, or Thirty Thousand Pounds, at the most: And, upon Inspection of the Transfer Books of that time, as well as upon the Examination of the before-mentioned Persons, your Committee cannot find any Transfers made by the Company of any part of that great Quantity of Stock, at the times specified in the Cashbook, excepting to the Duke of Portland, the Lord De la Wm\ and the honourable John West Esquire, who sold their Annuities to the Company; and no Account of any Transfers of such Stock has as yet been given in to this House; although, by your Order of the Seventeenth 6f December last, it was expressly required.

Upon farther Examination of the Persons before mentioned, your Committee discovered, That this supposed Sale of Stock was colourabiy entered in the Book, for the Benefit of Persons whose Names were designed to be concealed, with Intention to make an Interest in favour Of the Company, and to facilitate the Acceptance of the South Sea Proposals, and the Passing of the Bill; which w ere at that time depending in Parliament: And, to that End, the late Sub and Deputy Governors, Sir John Blunt, Mr. Gibbon, Mr. Chester, and Mr. Houlditch, late Directors, who had the Care of soliciting the passing the Bill, together with Mr. Knight, the Cashier, had the Power of disposing of this Stock:

And the general Method by which this Practice was carried on, was thus;

This Stock w as set dow n as sold at several Days, and at several Prices, from One hundred and Fifty Pounds per Cent, to Three hundred Tw enty-five Pounds per Cent.; and w as, from those times, to be esteemed as taken in, or holden, by the Company, for the Benefit of the pretended Purchasers; although no mutual Agreement was then made, for the Delivery, or Acceptance, of the Stock at

A. 172

any certain time; and although tio Money was paid down, nor any Deposit or other Security given to the Company for Payment, by the supposed Purchasers: So that if the Price of Stock had fallen, as might be expected if the Scheme had miscarried, no Loss could have been sustained by them; but if the Price of Stock should advance, as it actually did by the Success of the Scheme, the Difference by the advanced Price was to be made good to the pretended Purchasers: And, accordingly, the Account of such Stock was made up, and adjusted, with Mr. Knight4, and the Money arising by the Difference of the Price, between the Times of such taking in, or holding, the Stock, and the making such Adjustments, was paid or allowed, out of the Company’s Cash, to the pretended Purchasers:

But no entries of such Adjustments; or of the Names of the Persons with wrhom the same were made, appear to your Committee, in any of the Books of the Company.

Sir Theodore Jansscj: affirmed, That when the said Account in the Cash-book was laid, by Mr. Knight, before, their Committee of Treasury, to be passed and signed; an Objection being made, that Blanks were left lor the Names of the Buyers of this Stock, the late Sub Governor, and Mr. Knight, said, There were Reasons for passing the Account in that manner; and that the Stock was disposed of to Persons whose Names were not proper to' be known to a great many; but, at a lit time, a jjertect Account thereof should he made up; and that, if the Bill di$ pass, the Stock would be well sold.

Your Committee, in this Place, observe, That the Two Sums of Two hundred and two thousand Two hundred and Thirty Pounds, and Forty-seven thousand Seven hundred and Seventy Pounds, amount to Two hundred and fifty thousand Pounds: which, being added to the One hundred and twenty-five thousand Pounds, the supposed Price of the said Fifty thousand Pounds Stock, amounts to the whole Sum charged in the said Stock-ledger; viz* Three hundred and seventy-five thousand Pounds, as the Produce of the said Stock, upon the 1 ith of June 1720; and, deducting out of the Three hundred and seventy-five thousand Pounds the Sum of One hundred and twenty-five thousand Pounds for the Prime Cost of the said Stock, there remains a clear Difference of Two hundred and fifty thousand Pounds accruing to the Person for whose Benefit the Fifty thousand Pounds Stock was charged as sold in the Company’s Cash-book; which is the exact Amount of the Two Cash-notes made payable to Charles Stanhope Esquire, and accordingly entered, paid, and satisfied, unto him, on the 12th of December 1720:

In Confirmation of which Payment, it appears to your Committee, by the Drawing Cash-ledger, Letter K, now kept by Turner, Caszvall, and Sawbridge, in a new Copartnership with Mr. Henry Blunt, Son of Sir John Blunt, and Mr. Robinson Knight, Nephew of Mr. Robert 3

Knight, which Commenced the 25th of June 1720, Fol. 512. and 570. in an Account kept between Turner, Caszvall, and Sawbridge> and the new Copartners, That the said Tw'o hundred and fifty thousand Pounds was entered Paid, in Discharge of the Two Notes, upon the 12th of December 1720, and placed to the Account of Money disbursed upon the separate Account of Turner, Casxvall, and Sawbridge, out of their separate Cash actually paid into the Hands of the new Copartners, upon the 25th of June 1720; amounting, in real Cash, unto the Sum of One million One hundred sixty-six thousand Eight hundred seventy-five Pounds Four Shillings and One Peny; out of which the Two hundred and Fifty thousand Pounds are accordingly set off*, in Discharge of the new Copartners.

Your Committee examined John Mount and John Muddy, Cashiers to Turner and Company, as well before, as since, the new Copartnership; Richard Fenton, their Book-keej>er; and also Jacob Sawbridge junior, Son of Jacob Sazvbridge inquire; the said Robinson Knight and Henry Blunt, who, before the 2.5th of June 1720, were Assistants in the Office of Turner and Company; relating to the said several Books and Entries, and to the said transactions therein contained: And John Mount, John Muddys and Richard Fenton,'declared, That they verily believed, that all the said Accounts and Entries of lie? ceipts and Payments, and of issuing and paying Notes, were true; and that the respective Sums mentioned therein to have been received and paid, were really received and paid; and that the Notes therein mentioned to have been issued and paid, were actually issued and paid according to the Import of the several Entries; and that these Two Notes for Tw o hundred and two thousand Two hundred and Thirty Pounds, and Forty-seven thousand Seven hundred and Seventy Pounds, were actually issued, payable to Charles Stanhope Esquire, upon the 11th of June 1720, in the usual and regular Manner; the Note for Two hundred and tw'o thousand Two hundred and Thirty Pounds being entered, and filled up, by the said Henry Blunt; and the other Note for Forty-seven thousand Seven hundred and Seventy Pounds being entered, and filled up, by Jacob Sazvbridge junior, by the Direction of Jacob Sazvbridge senior, Esquire; and both the Notes signed by Robinson Knight, then entrusted by Turner and Company to sign Notes for them, as Jacob Sawbridge junior, Robinson Knight, and Henry Blunt, did acknowledge; and that Turner and Company did thereby become chargeable with the Payment of the Money mentioned in the Two Notes; and that the Two Notes were actually paid and satisfied upon the 12th of December 1720, according to the Entries thereof made in the said Books, out of the Cash, amounting to One million One hundred sixty six thousand Eight hundred Seventy-five Pounds Four Shillings and One Peny, really paid, and answered, by Turner, Casxvall, and Sawbridge, into the newCopartnership (which Henry Blunt and Robinson Knight, the new Copartners did likewise confess); and that the Two Notes being then discharged, were delivered up to Turner and Company.

Here your Committee *ust observe, That in the Account of Stock sold, laid before this House, they find the Names of several Members of this House, and of the House of Peers, not concerned in the Administration, or in the Management, of the publick Revenue; whose Cases your Committee could not particularly examine, but must wait for the Consideration and Direction of the House, in what manner such Examination shall proceed: In the mean time your Committee think it proper to acquaint the House with divers Practices made Use of to raise the nominal Value of South Sea Stock to that extravagant Rate to which it was afterwards advanced, above the real and intrinsick Value thereof.

Your Committee find, That, by Computations made by the Direction of your Committee, it appears, that the Directors of the South Sea Company might have raised the whole Sum stipulated for the Publick, with a Profit of near One million and a Half, for the Benefit of the Proprietors of the old Stock, without setting their Stock to Sale at any higher Price than 150 per Cent.;

That, after the said Directors had taken in the First Money Subscription at Three hundred per Cent. and the Second Money Subscription at Four hundred Pounds per Cent. and the First Subscription of the long and short Annuities at £. 375. per Cent, the Value of One hundred Pounds South Sea Stock was but £. 120. or thereabouts; supposing the whole Money of the said First and Second Subscriptions, amounting to Twelve millions Seven hundred and Fifty thousand Pounds, had been all paid in: That the said Court of Directors did afterwards proceed to take in a Third and a Fourth Money Subscription, at the Rate of One thousand Pounds per Centum; and a Second Subscription of the Long and Short Annuities, and a Subscription of the redeemable Debts, at the Rate of Eight hundred Pounds per Cent.; after which, the Value of One hundred Pounds South Sea Stock was but Three hundred Thirty-two Pounds, or thereabouts; supposing the whole Money of the said Four Money Subscriptions, amounting to Sixty-eight millions Seven hundred and fifty thousand Pounds, had been all paid in:

That if all the remaining publick Debts had been taken in, and all the remaining Stock of the Company sold, on the Terms which the said Directors pretended to expect, £. 100. South Sea Stock would have been worth but £. $47. or thereabouts; supposing the Money of the said Four Subscriptions, and the Money for the remaining Stock, which, together, would have amounted to Two hundred and Five millions Thirty-nine thousand Four hundred and One Pounds, had been ail paid in:

That on the Thirtieth Day of August last the Court of Directors of the South Sea Company came to a Resolution, which on the 8th Day of September last was confirmed by a General Court, to declare a Dividend of Thirty Pounds per Centum to be made at Christmas 1720; and of not less than Fifty Pounds per Centum per Annum for not less than Twelve Years to come from that time: That soon after this Resolution, viz. at a General Court held the Twentieth Day of September last, the Sub Governor acquainted the General Court, That the Affairs of the Company, in relation to the Price of their Stock, and Subscriptions, had taken an unexpected Turn; and thereupon proposed their giving a Power to the Court of Directors to relieve the last Subscribers of the publick Debts, and the Proprietors of the Two last Money Subscriptions; which was accordingly granted: And at a Court of Directors held the 29th Day of September last, it was resolved, That the said Subscribers should have the same Terms with the Bank; viz. That their Subscriptions should be reduced from One thousand Pounds, and Eight hundred Pounds, per Centum, to Four hundred Pounds; and that they should also have the Benefit of the Midsummer Dividend of Ten Pounds per Cent.; which was accordingly confirmed by a General Court held the Thirtieth Day of the same Month: Upon which, your Committee observe, That it appears to them very extraordinary, That the Directors, on the Eighth Day of September when the said high Dividend was declared in a Ge-VpL. 19.

ueral Court, should have had a© Foresight of the Tufti Sooth which so soon after, viz, on the 20th Day of the same Month, happened in their Affairs:

That on the said Eighth Day of September' the Sub Governor acquainted the General Court, That their Directors had been unanimous in all their Proceedings.; which,.amongst other Things, includes the before-mentioned several Subscriptions by them taken in, except the First: And, upon the Examination of the Directors, it doth not appear to your Committee, that any one of them protested against, or declared any publick Disserit from, any of the said Proceedings; and it appears, that all of them took their Shares ana Proportions of the Subscriptions which were allotted for the respective Directors to dispose of.

And your Committee have been informed by Sir Theodore Janssen, That there was a Meeting at the House of Sir John Fellou es, betw ixt Sixteen of the Court of Directors, and Mr. Secretary Craggs, and Mr. Aislabie; at which time it was proposed, That a Subscription should be taken in at £. 300. per Cent.; which was approved of by Mr. Secretary Craggs and Mr. Aislabie; and that, when the said Company broke up, it was agreed, That every one should use their best Endeavours to promote it; which is confirmed by the Information of Sir Lambert Blackwell:

And at a Court of Directors, held the 13th Day of April last, it was resolved to take in a Subscription for Two millions, at the Rate of Three hundred Pounds per Centum; but the same was afterwards increased, without any previous Resolution to that Purpose, to Two millions Two hundred and Fifty thousand Pounds: And your Committee observe, That the imaginary Value of the said Subscriptions rose very fast; and that those who had the Benefit of the said additional Subscription, if they sold and disposed of the same, made very great Gams thereby.

That at a Court of Directors, held the 28th Day of April last, it was resolved to take in a Second Money Subscription, at the Rate of £. 400. per Cent, for One million; but, by the Accounts delivered in to this House, it appears, that the said Subscription was for One milliCni Five hundred thousand Pounds; yet it doth not appear, that there was any previous Resolution of the Court of Directors for the Addition of Five hundred thousand Pounds; nor was the said Addition declared till the 8th Day of September last; at which time the Sub Governor acquainted the General Court therewith: Upon which, your Committee cannot but observe the great Distance of Time between the taking in of the Second Subscription at One million, and the Eighth Day of September when the same w as reported to the General Court at One million Five hundred thousand Pounds; during which Interval the imaginary Value of that Subscription was excessively increased; whereby the Persons w ho had the same, had the Advantage of that extraordinary Rise.

That at a Court of Directors, held the Fifteenth Day of June last, it was resolved to take in a Third Money Subscription, at the Rate of One thousand Pounds per Centum; One-tenth Part whereof was to be paid down at the time of Subscribing: And at a Court of Directors, held the 23d Day of the same Month, the Sub Governor acquainted the Court, That the said Third Money Subscription was completed, without mentioning to what Sum; but at the before-mentioned General Court, held the 8th Day of September last, he declared the same to be for Five millions: And Mr. Knight, late Cashier of the South Sea Company, by an Article dated the 20th Day of June last, in the Cash-book, Fol. 125. charges the said Sum of Five millions as received; which Account was passed, and allowed, by the Company’s Committee of Treasury, on, or sometime after, the Fourth Day of August last; and yet, in the Account of the Third Money Subscription, delivered in to this House, it is stated at Four millions Four hundred thousand Pounds only; the remaining Sum of Six hundred thousand Pounds being entered on the Credit-side of the same Cash-book, on the 19th Day of December 1720, as a supposed Defi-5 S ciencf

ciency of the Payments on this Subscription; although it appears to your Committee, upon the Evidence of Mr. Lockyer, and others, that not only the whole Sum of Five millions, but even a considerable exceeding thereon, was paid in; that a great deal of Money was repaid back, to reduce the Subscription to Five millions; and that they had Money enough paid in for near Eight millions.

That at a Court of Directors, held the 12th Day of August last, it was resolved to take in a Fourth Money Subscription for One million, at the rate of One thousand Poundspa%Centum: And at a Court of Directors, held the 2 jth Day of the same Month, it was declared, That, upon -casting up the Books, it was found, that the said Fourth Money Subscription, instead of One million, was increased to One million Two hundred and Fifty thousand Pounds»; which was occasioned by taking the said Subscriptions in several Books; and at the before-mentioned General Court, held the Eighth Day of September last, the Sub Governor declared the Fourth Money Subscription was completed to One million Two hundred and Fifty thousand Pounds: And Mr. Knight, the Cashier, hath, in an Article, dated the Thirtieth Day of August last, and entered in the Cash-Book, Folio 128, given the Company Credit for the First Payment, made on the Fourth Subscription; viz. For Two millions Five hundred thousand Pounds: which Account was passed, and allowed, by their Committee of Treasury, on the Fourth Day of October; and vet, in the Account of the said Fourth Money Subscription, delivered into this I louse, it is stated at One million Two hundred thousand Pounds only:

That, upon the Examination of Mr. Knight, and several of the Directors, in relation to the Deficiency of the said Third and Fourth Money Subscriptions, their Answers were very unsatisfactory; and your Committee cannot but observe, That as, by the before-mentioned Additions to the First Two Money Subscriptions, some Persons made great Gains whilst the Price of the said Subscriptions continued high, so, when the Price of the Subscriptions fell, many other Persons were favoured, by having their Subscriptions..withdrawn, which was the Cause of the Deficiency.

That, on the Second Money Subscription, each Director was allowed, for himself and Friends, Twenty-six thousand Pounds; and that the Remainder of the Million, at first resolved to be taken in, was at the Disposal of the Sub and Deputy Governors; but for whose Benefit the additional Subscription of Five hundred thousand Pounds was intended, your Committee have not yet been able to discover:

That, on the Third Money Subscription, each Director was allowed Fifty-four thousand Pounds, for himself and Friends; and that several large Lists of Names of Persons were sent to the Sub Governor to be admitted into . the said Third Subscription; viz. by the Earl of Sunde)'-land, First Lord Commissioner of the Treasury, a List, amounting to One hundred Sixty-seven thousand Pounds; by John Aislabie Esquire, late Chancellor of the Exchequer, another of the Lords of the Treasury, a List, amount-; ing to Seventy-five thousand Three hundred Pounds; by James, Graggs Esquire, one of his Majesty’s principal Secretaries of State, Two Lists, amounting to Six hundred Ninety-five thousand Pounds; and by Charles Stanhope Esquire, One of the Secretaries of the Treasury, a List, amounting to Forty-nine thousand Seven hundred Pounds; which Four last mentioned Lists amount to Nine hundred Eighty-seven thousand Pounds:

That, upon Examination, it appears, That other Lists have been given in as well 011 the Third as on the Second Subscription; but, the same being lost or mislaid, as your Committee have been informed, they are thereby disabled at present from making any Report thereon: They find Twenty-five thousand Pounds of the Second Subscription to have been given to John Aislabie Esquire, about Eight or Ten Days after the Opening of that Subscription, at which time the Subscriptions were at an advanced Price of about £. 40. per Cent.; and sqqu after rose vastly higher.

That it doth not appear favour Committee, That any of the Persons who had the Honour to serve his Majesty in the Treasury, or in any other Part of the Administration, used any Endeavours to prevent the Directors of the South Sea Company from taking in Subscriptions at the aforesaid extravagant Prices: But, on the contrary, it doth appear, That some of *them, by the Lists they gave in, as aforesaid, did not only encourage and promote the said Subscriptions, but greatly enlarge the same.

Your Committee observing, That Sir John FcHgiccs, late Sub Governor of the South Sea Company, did, at a General Court of the said Company, held the Twenty-first Day of April 1720, acquaint that Court, That the Design of the Governments Million of Exchequer Bills to be lent to the Company, by virtue of the late Act of Parliament for issuing Exchequer Bills, to be circulated at or near the Exchequer, was to enable the Company to lend Money upon their Stock; and finding that, by Order of the Court of Directors of the said Company, the same had been so lent out; your Committee proceeded to enquire into this Affair:

And, on the Examination of Mr. Robert Knight, late Cashier of the said Company, lie declared, That he did not remember, that-any Application was made by the Directors to have those Bills issued; but that the First Discourse of this Matter was by John Aislabie Esquire, then Chancellor of the Exchequer, about a Week before the Proposals of the South Sea Company were offered to this House: And that Mr. Aislabie said, It would be moreao ceptable to have those Bills circulated at the Exchequer, than to send them to the Bank, or elsewhere; and that the Company might afford to circulate them for nothing, they being to be lent to the Company to enable them to execute their Scheme: That the Examinant believed the Intention of lending the said Bills upon Stock had been communicated to Mr. Aislabie] and that he, the Examinant, on his attending on the Treasury to solicit the issuing of these Bills, did. mention that Design; and never heard, that the Treasury disapproved of it: That Sir John Blunt declared, It would be better to employ these Bills in the lending upon Stock, than in paying off the lledeemables, which would take up more time.

Hereupon, your Committee examining Sir John Fd-lozces, he said, That lie, and others of the Directors, treated, with Mr. Aislabie, and others, at the Treasury, about the issuing the said Exchequer Bills; but that it was first proposed to Mr. Aislabie; and the Examinant believed it was at first mentioned by Sir John Blunt, in a Committee of the Directors; and that it was the general Opinion of the Directors.

Your Committee examining Sir John Blunt as to this -Transaction, he declared, that he spoke to Mr. Aislabie to hasten the issuing of the said Bills; and, that himself, or some other of the Directors, acquainted Mr. Jislabic, as he believes, at the Treasury, with the NCompany's Design to lend them upon Stock; that it did not at first arise from the Directors, but that it was intimated to them before, or very soon after, the Company's Proposals were laid before the I louse, by some of the Treasury; and, on Recollection, the Examinant said, It was by Mr. Aislabie, to enable the Company to carry on their Scheme; and thereby to raise the Price of the Stock, the Borrowers being enabled to buy Stock.

That, by the Book of Loans, delivered in to this IJouse, it appears. That the Sum of Nine millions Thirty-nine thousand Nine hundred Thirty-six Pounds Eleven Shillings was lent to several Persons, on the Security of Two millions Five hundred Sixty-three thousand One hundred and Seventeen Pounds Seventeen Shillings and Five Pence. Copies of the several Resolutions of the General Court, and Court of Directors, of the South Sea Company, relating to Loans.

At a General Court held the 2ist April 1720. Resolved, Nemine contradicente, That the Court of Directors be, and are hereby, impowered, from time to time, as they shall see for the Interest of the Company, to lend any Sum or Sums of the Company's Money on the Company’s present, and to be increased, Capital Stock; and to do all such Matters and Things as they shall judge most for the Good of the Company.

At a Court of Directors, 21 Apr. 1720.

Resolved, That the Sub and Deputy Governors, and Committee of the Treasury, be, and are hereby im-

Sowered to lend any Sutn or Sums of the Company’s loney, not exceeding £. 500,000. in the Whole, upon Security of Capital Stock in this Company.

Resolved, That the Money which should be so lent, do not exceed £. 250. on every £. 100. Stock.

Resolved, That the Money so to be lent do not exceed £. 5,000. to any One Person; and that the same run at £.,rj. per Cent. per Annum Interest, and be for any Time, not exceeding Four Months.

At a Court of Directors, the 20th May 1720* Ordered, That it be referred to the Sub and Deputy Governors, and Committee of the Treasury, as soon as the Company are possessed of the Exchequer Bills, to lend out such Sums thereof as they shall think convenient, upon the Stock of this Company, at the Rate of £300. upon every £. 100. Stock, and at an Interest of £.4. per Cent, per Annum, for such Time as they shall think fit, not exceeding Six Months.

Ordered, That it be an Instruction to the Sub and Deputy Governors, and Committee of the Treasury,.That they do not lend to any One Person more than £.3,060.

At a Court of Directors, 9th June 1720.

Ordered That it be referred to the Committee of South Sed Treasury to prepare forthwith the Form of the Defeazance Company to be executed, for all Money lent, or to be lent, on the Company's Stock.

Ordered, That it be a Direction to the Company’s Cashier, That upon Receipt of the principal Money which the Company have lent, or shall lend, on the Stock of the Company, and the Interest to the Time of Repayment, that the Cashier re-transfer the Stock, on the usual Transfer-days, notwithstanding the Time for which the Money was borrowed be not expired.

Ordered, That it be an Instruction to the Committee of Treasury, That they do not lend to any One Person exceeding £. 4,000. upon the Company’s Stock, at £. 400. per Cent.

At a Court of Directors, 27th July 1720.

Resolved, That it be referred to the Committee of Treasury to lend to any of the Proprietors of the First Subscription Receipts, the Third Payment, which becomes due the 25th of August next; and to the Proprietors of the Second Subscription Receipts, the Second Payment, which becomes due the 14th of September next j for Six Months, at an Interest of £. 4. per Cent, per Annum; and that they also consider of a Method of lending the same: And that such Persons as borrow, may have a Liberty to repay the Money borrowed before the Time limited, if they desire the same; and the Interest to cease on the Day of such Repayment.

Ordered, That it be referred to the said Committee to lend or employ the Company’s Money, that is, or shall be, in Cash, between this and Michaelmas next, in such manner as shall be judged most for the Company’s Interest.

Resolutions relating to South Sea Directors.

Tlte House proceeded to take the said Report into Consideration.

Resolved\ Nemine contradicentex That the date Sub Governor, Deputy Governor, and Directors of the South Sea Company, and their Officers, and their Aiders and Abettors, in leriding out the Companies Money upon Stock, and Subscriptions, withorit taking sufficient Security for Repayment thereof, have been guilty of a notorious Breach of Trust; and have thereby occasioned great Loss to the Company; for which they ought 16 make Satisfaction out of their own Estates.

ResolvedNemine contradicente, That the Selling or Disposing of Stock, or Subscriptions, transferred or deposited as a Security for the Repayment of the Motley s6 lent, was a notorious Breach of the Trust reposed in the said Sub Governor; Deputy Governor, Directors, rind their Officers; and a Fraud on the Proprietors, in order to enrich themselves; for which they ought to make Satisfaction out of their own Estates.

Resolved, Nemine contradicente, That the Taking in, of Holding of Stock, by the South Sea Company, for the Benefit of any Member of either House of Parliament, or Person concerned in the Administration (during the time that the Company’s Proposals, or the Bill thereto relating, were depending in Parliament,) without any valuable Consideration paid, or sufficient Security given, for the Acceptance of, or Payment for such Stock, and the Company’s paying or allowing such Person the Difference arising by the advanced Price of the Stocks, were corrupt, infamous, and dangerous, Practices, highly reflecting on the Honour and Justice of Parliaments, and destructive of the Interest of his Majesty’s Government.

A Message from the Lords, by Mr. Ilolford and Mr.

Lovibcnd:

Mr. Speaker,

We are commanded by the Lords to acquaint this House, That their Lordships, intending to take into Consideration, on Monday next, some Matters, relating to a Tryal at the last Assizes at Hereford, touching the Presentation to the Vicarage of Leominster, desire, That Sir George Casual!, a Member of tUs House, may have Leave to attend the House of Lords, to declare his Knowledge concerning the same.

And thfcn the Messengers withdrew*.

Ordered, That Sir George Casual! have Leave to attend the Lords, as is desired by thieir Lordships, if he thinks fit.

And the Messengers were called in again; and Mr. Speaker acquainted them, That the House had considered: their Message, arid had gi ven Leave to Sir George Casmdl to attend the Lords, as their Lordships desire, if he thinks fit.

Resolved, Nemjne contradicente, That any of the Directors of the South Sea Company selling their own Stock at high Prices to the Company, or other's, at the same time that they gave Orders for buying Stock upon Account of the Company, under Pretence of keeping upr the nominal Value of the said Stock, w:as a scandalous Practice, tending to enrich themselves, to the great Loss and Detriment of the Company, and of others his Majesty's Subjects; for which they ought to make Satisfaction out of their Own Estates.

'Resolved, Nemine contradicente, That the declaring a Dividend of-Thirty per Cent, for Christmas last, and not less than Fifty pci' Cent .* per Annum for notices than Twelve Yeats after, was an infamous Contrivance to give his Majesty’s Subjects false Notions of the Value of the’ said Stock, that the late Directors might more easily dispose of their own Stock at exorbitant Prices.

Resolved, Nemine contradicente, That the setting the Stock of the South Sea Company to Sale by Subscriptions, at high Prices, above the intrinsick Value of the same, by the late Sub Governor, Deputy Governor, and Direo, tors, of the said Company, was a gross and notorious Fraud; and has been one great Cause of the sinking of the publick Credit, and bringing upon the N ation the Distress it at present labours under, -

Vql. 19.

'Resolved\ Nemine contradicente, That the advising the late Sub Governor, Deputy Governor, and Directors of t t\ie South Sea Company, to set the Stock of the said Company to Sale by Subscriptions, at high and extravagant Prices; or 10 declare the high and extravagant Dividends for Chi'istmas last, and Twelve Years after/by any Persons in the Administration: was a notorious Breach of the Trust reposed in them; to the Prejudice of his Majesty Government, and the Interest of this Kingdom.

Ordered, That the further Chhsideration of the said Report be adjourned till Tuesday Morning next.

Arid then the House adjourned till Monday Morning, Nine of the Clock.

He was called in; ancf presented to the House a Paper, containing the Proceedings and Resolutions of the General Court of the South Sea Company, held the Twenty-third of December 1720.

And then he withdrew.

The Title of the said Paper was read.

The said Paper of the Proceedings and Resolutions of the General Court is as follows; viz.

To the honourable the Commons of Great Britain in Parliament assembled.

IN Obedience to an Order of this honourable House, of the 21st of this instant February, the Directors of the South Sea Company lay before you the Proceedings and Resolutions of the General Court of the said Company, held the 23d Decevdier last; which are as follow; viz. Friday 23d December 1720.

At a General Court of the South Sea Company, held at Merchant Taylors-hall.

The Minutes of the last General Court were read. The Sub Governor opened the Court in manner following;

Gentlemen,

The Occasion of calling this General Court is to acquaint you with what was opened on Wednesday last in the honourable House of Commons, in relation to this Company; which, as w e are informed, was to the Effect following; viz.

1. That the First Money Subscription be completed; allowing longer Time for future Payments, and making them less, or more easy; or that Stock be given for the Money already paid in, or due, for the First Four Payments upon this Subscription; as shall be hereafter determined by a General Court.

2. That for the Money paid, and due, on the Second ‘Subscription, and for the Monies paid on the Third and Fourth Money Subscriptions, there be Stock in this Company allowed to the respective Proprietors, after the Rate of 400 per Cent, together with 10 per Cent. for, or in lieu of, the last Midsummer Dividend; and that the future Payments, to become due on those Subscriptions, be discharged.

3. That the Stock belonging to the Company, which shall then remain undispos^ of} amounting to about

Vo l. 19.

£.11,600,000. be divided out, in Capital, to all the Proprietors of Stock, as w-ell by Subscription as otherwise; which would amount to about 45 per Cent, upon every Proprietor’s present Stock: But it is proposed, That the ascertaining the exact Quantum that is to be carried to each Proprietors Account, be reserved to the future Determination of a General Court.

4. That a Sum, not exceeding £. g,000,000. Part of this Company’s original, and increased, and to be increased, Capital Stock, be ingrafted into the Capital Stock of the Bank of England, on Terms to be agreed on between this Company and the Bank.

5. That a Sum, likewise, not exceeding Nine millions, Part of this Company’s original, and increased, and to be increased, Capital Stock, be ingrafted also into the Capital Stock of the East India Company, on Terms to be agreed on between this Company and the East India Company.

6. It is proposed, That for the Stock, to be thus ingrafted on the Bank, and East India Company, each of those Companies are to have an Annuity out of the Company’s Funds, after the Rate of 5 per Cent, per Annum, to attend the same, together with £. 2,000. per Annum to each of those Companies, out of this Company’s Allowance, for Charges of Management:

7. That about One-fourth Part of each Proprietor’s Stock, after the Addition made to his Capital, be w rit into the Bank; and about One-fourth Part more thereof into the East India Company, to make up the said Sums, not exceeding Nine millions, to be ingrafted into each of the said Companies: And the Capital Stock of those Companies may be enlarged so much as the w hole Sum of this Company’s Stock, to be ingrafted into each Company, shall amount to; and the particular Proprietors of this Company to have Credit in the Stock of the Bank, and of the East India Company, after the Rate of £. 120 per Cent, for the Stock of those companies; wrhereby, if the Sum ingrafted into the Bank be just Nine millions, there will belong to the Proprietors of this Company, in Bank Stock, £.7,500,000.: and there will remain to the Bank, for the Common Use and Benefit of all the Proprietors, as wc\\ of the to be ingrafted, as of the present, Stock, £.1,500,000. Stock, in their Corporate Capacities.

8. And for the Nine millions to be ingrafted into the East India Company, there will also belong to the Proprietors of this Company £.7,500,000. Stock; and there will remain to the East Inaia Company, in their Corporate Capacity also, £.1,500,000. Stock; whereof £.640,000. is proposed to be for the Benefit of the Proprietors of the present Stock of that Company; and the remaining £.860,000. Stock, for the Common Use and Benefit of the Proprietors, as well of the to be ingrafted, as of the present, Stock of this Company:

9. That all the Profits which have hitherto arisen, or shall arise, to this Company, by increasing their Capital, by taking in the publick Debts and Incumbrances, or by Money Subscriptions, or otherwise, shall remain for the sole Benefit of the Stock which shall remain in this Company, after the said Ingraftments; as shall likewise all future Privileges and Advantages to be granted by the Publick to this Company.

Gentlemen,

Your Court of Directors, having taken under their Consideration your Resolution concerning the Delivery of the Receipts, at 400 per Cent, for the Third and Fourth Money Subscriptions made into this Company, have, in order to comply therewith, advised with several eminent Counsel; but, as they find it a Matter of great Importance to the Corporation, they have desired further Time to consider of this Affair: And your Court of Directors do assure you, they will not issue the Receipts, unless in Compliance with the Directions of a future General Court.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this General Court, That no Receipts be given out for the Third and Fourth Money Subscriptions, unless by the Approbation and Directions of the General Court: And in case the present 6 A Scheme

45 s 230 — -240 Februarii. . 1720.

Scheme is approved of, that then the Stock shall be carried to the Account of the Subscribers, in lieu of their Subscriptions.

Resolved, That the Court of Directors be, and are hereby, impowered to make a Proposal to the honourable House of Commons, upon the foot of the Proposition now read.

Resolved, That the Court of Directors be, and are hereby impowered to treat with the East India Company, and Bank of England, in relation to the said Proposal; and that they lay the same before the General Court for their Approbation.

Then, upon a Question, the Court adjourned.

By Order of the Court of Directors,

South Sea House, D. JVescomb, Secretary.

That the Committee, pursuant to the Order of the House, have examined the Matter of the said Petition; and find, upon examining Mr. Jacob Smith, who testified,

When the said Act was first put in Execution the said Highways were in so bad and ruinous a Condition, that, in order to the carrying the Undertaking on with Success, the Commissioners borrowed the Sum of £. 3,000. bn the Credit of the Tolls, as they were, by the said Act, impowered to do; and engaged the Income and Profits of the several Tolls, for Repayment thereof, with Interest for the same.

That it appeared to the Committee, by the Accounts kept of the Money received and paid on Account of the Tolls, since the passing of the said Act, That the said £.3,000. so borrowed, as also what other Money has,-from time to time, been collected at the several Turnpikes, has been constantly laid out in paying the Interest of the Money so borrowed, and towards repairing the Highways, and other necessary Works directed to be done by the said Act:

That, a great Part of the Term granted by the said former Act being expired, the Creditors on the said Tolls have brought their Bill in the Court of Chancery, to have the Profits of the said Tolls applied towards discharging their Mortgage-money; and have lately obtained a Decree That the Profits of the several Tolls shall be applied to repay their Principal and Interest accordingly:

That, the Sum of Six hundred Pounds being only paid of the Money so borrowed, there still remains due on the said Mortgage the Sum of £.2,400. whkhcarries Interest after the Rate of Six Pounds Cent, per Annum,

It appeared to the Committee, That there is Part of the Road between the said City of Bath and Bristol, and also between Bath and Tiverton in the said County, about Two Miles in Length, adjoining to some Parts of the Roads directed to be repaired by the said former Act, and near the City of Bath, much out of Repair; and that the same cannot be amended and kept in Repair by the ordinary Course of the Laws now in being:

Your Committee also found, on the Examination of Mr. JFymo tide sold and John Falconbridge, That several Parcels of South Sea Stock, amounting to Twenty thousand Pounds Stock, were bought by Mr. Wymondesold, for Mr. Aislabie, on the First of March 1719, at several Prices, amounting to Thirty-five thousand Three hundred Fifty-seven Pounds Ten Shillings; and that Mr. Knight, late Cashier of the South Sea Company, paid the Examinant the Money for such Stock, and placed the same to Mr. Aislabies Account: Mr. Wymondesold produced to your Committee a Letter, from Mr. Aislabie to him, dated the First of March 1719; whereby he directs Mr. Wymondesold to buy this Twenty thousand Pounds Stock; and adds, That he would desire Mr. Knight to pay the Money for the said Stock: Which Letter, the Examinant said, is of the Hand-writing of Mr. Aislabie, and was received by the Examinant on the said First of March; and the Examinant returned an Answer to Mr. Aislabie oh the same Day: That, on the Fourth of March last, Mr, Knight adjusted the said Stock with the Examinant Wymondesold, who delivered the Stock to Mr. Knight, For the Use of Mr. Aislabie; and Mr. Knight paid the Examinant the Money for such Stock.

John Falconbridge, who was concerned in the entering, and making out the Accounts kept, of this Stock, being examined, said, That about a Fortnight since, and after 'Mr. Wymondesold's First Examination before the House of , Peers, and his delivering in an Account of Stock bought for Mr. Aislabie, by Mr. Wymondesold\ to your Committee; Mr. Aislabie requiring the Particulars of the Stock bought and sold for him by Mr. Wymondesold, the Examinant, by Mr. Wymondesold's Direction, attended Mr. Aislabie with the Particulars thereof: That Mr. Aislabie then objected against the said Twenty thousand Pounds Stock, bought the First of March; and, with Execrations hot fit to be repeated, declared, He knew nothing of it; and bid the Examinant tell Mr. Wymondesold\ that he, Mr. Aislabie, must declare the same, upon Oath, at the Bar of the House: The Examinant then told him, That he happened to object against an Article which was the plainest in his Account; for that this very Twenty thousand Pounds Stock was taken in for him, and paid for by Mr. Knight; and that the Examinant had shewn the same Article to Mr. Waller, Mr. Aislabie s Son-in-law, in an Account made up, and settled, with Mr. Knight, long since; which Mr. Waller, who was then present, said, was true: And the Examinant, the next Day, attending ’Mr. Aislabie, with the Explanation of the Account, on Sight of it, Mr. Aislabie expressed himself thus; viz. " Aye, this " makes it plainer; now I can. recollect something of it."

The said Mr. Wymondesold further informed your Committee, That there were Dealings between Mr. Aislabie and Mr. Knight; and that the Examinant had seen a Green Book in Mr, Knight's Custody, wherein the Account of Mr. Aislabie was kept; which Green Book your Committee apprehended to be the same Book mentioned in the Examination of Mr. Surman, taken Notice of in their former Report.

Mr. Hazves further acquainted your Committee, That he had Dealings in Stock with Mr. Aislabie, for a considerable time past, and kept an Account of the same in a Book, of which Mr. Aislabie had a Duplicate: That the Accounts in the said Books were continued till some time in November last; and that, upon every Adjustment, Mr. Aislabie and the Examinant usually signed each others Book: That, amongst other tilings, the said Books contained Accounts of Quantities of South Sea Stock, bought and sold by the Examinant for Mr. Aislabie: That, some time in November last, the Accounts were finally settled, and adjusted, between them; and thereupon the Examinant was ordered, by Mr. Aislabie, to bring the Book, which the Examinant kept, to Mr. Aislabie; which he accordingly did; and then Mr. Aislabie desired to have it delivered up to him: Which, at first, the Examinant was

*5

unwilling to do, saying, That he ought to keep it for his own Justification: But Mr. Aislabie told him, That, the Account being then made up between them, he would have the Book up, that Nobody else might see it: And Mr. Aislabie gave the Examinant a Receipt in full of alL Demands; and the Examinant delivered him the Book: Mr. Hazves further said, That he never was desired so to do, nor ever did the like to any Person with whom he had Dealings of this Nature.

Your Committee have been informed, by Mr. Robert Simnan, That several Sums of Money were paid, out of ths Company’s Cash, to John Aislabie Esquire: And, by the Book of Cash Draughts, kept between the South Sea Company and the Bank, and also by the said Mr. Surman s Examination, your Committee find, That, on the 18th of April 1720, a Bill for Twenty-seven thousand Three hundred Seventy-eight Pounds Nineteen Shillings and Six Pence was drawn by Mr. Knight, then Cashier of the South Sea Company, upon the Bank of England, payable to the said Mr. Aislabie; and the Entry of the said Bill in the Cash Draught-book, has been since razed by Mr. Knight' sDirection: Who told Mr. Surman, That he had taken that Bill back again in Payment; and, as the Examinant believed, from Mr. Aislabie: That a Bill for the further Sum of Six thousand Pounds was drawn the 1 tth of June >720, and paid, by the Bank, out of the Cash kept there, in the Name of the South Sea Company, to Mr. Aislabie, on the Tenth of September last; and the Sums of Four thousand Seven hundred Pounds, and Eighty-six Pounds, were, in like manner, drawn the 20th of September last; and paid to the said Mr. Aisla-hie on the First of October following.

Your Committee are still proceeding upon the Matters referred to them, in order to lay the same before the House.

A PETITION of the Mayor, capital Burgesses, and clandestiw XV Freemen, and also of the Merchants, and others, ^Iu‘rt*uoa trading in the Woollen Manufactures, within the Borough ot 'Vooi* of Camelford, in the County of Cornwall, and Places adjacent, was presented to the House, and read; setting forth,

That the great Support of that Town and Neighbourhood is the Woollen Manufacture, heretofore chiefly carried on with Irish Wool, transported in vast Quantities to Bide-ford\ in Devon, from whence they are supplied; but, of late, little or none hath been transported thither, by reason it is clandestinely run to France; so that they are enabled to under-sell us in foreign Markets; which, if not timely prevented, must inevitably prove the Ruin of our Woollen Manufacture: And praying Relief.

Ordered, That the said Petition do lie upon the Table.

SIR Hungerford Hoskins reported from the Commit- udbuty tee, to whom the Petition of the Inhabitants of thfe Roads. Parish, ancient Borough, and Town of Ledbury, witllih the County of Hereford, w as referred, the Matter as it appeared to them; and which they had directed him to report to the House; and he read the same in his Place; and afterwards delivered the Report in at the Clerks Table: Where the same was read; and is as follows; visa That the Committee, pursuant to the Ordpr of the House, have examined the Matter of the said Petition; and find,

That Ledbury is a great Market Town, and, some Years past, was mirch the best for Grain of all Sorts within the said County; situate in a deep Clay Country,

Twelve computed Miles distant from Gloucester, Ten from Woi'ccster, Ten from Hereford, Fifteen from Leominster,

Nine from Bromyard, Eight from Rosse, Nine from favkesbury, and Seven from Upton:

That, upon the Examination of Henry Jo?ics Esquire, the said Roads of late Years are become deep, and dangerous to Passengers, chiefly occasioned by great and heavy Carriages of Goods to and from the Rivers Severn and Wye; and that, in the Winter-time, it is impracticable for Waggons, Carriages, or Horses, loaden, to come to the said^rpwm, without manifest Danger and Hazard; and even in the Summer-season, at some times, some Places are impassable.

That it appeared to the Committee, That the Inhabitants have always done their Duty, as the Law prescribes; notwithstanding which great Sums are yearly raised towards the Amendments of the same, they are found very far deficient; and cannot be amended, and kept in Repair, without some other Provision for that Purpose.

The House proceeded, according to Order, to take into Consideration the Representation of the Lords Commissioners of Trade and Plantations, relating to the Prohibition of Callicoes; and proposing what Methods may be most proper and effectual for securing to the East India Company their carrying on successfully a Trade so beneficial to the Kingdom; which was laid before this House upon the First Day 01 February, pursuant to the Address of this House to his Majesty:

And the said Repiesention was read; and is as follows; ci-.

To the King’s most Excellent Majesty.

May it please your Majesty,

IN Obedience to the Commands of their Excellencies the1 late Lords Justices, signified to us, by Mr. Delafaye, the 24th of June last; directing us, pursuant to the Address of the House of Lords to your Majesty,

" That we should consider of, and propose, a Scheme,

" to laid before your Majesty, and both Houses of " Parliament, in the next Session of Parliament, for the " effectual preventing the wearing and using painted,

4t stained, and dyed, Callicoes, which are so detrimental lc to the Manufactures of this Kingdom; and also to u consider of, and state, the many Difficulties the East 14 India Company do at present lie under in the carrying " on of their Trade; and propose what Methods may be 14 most proper and effectual for securing to the said Corn-n pany their carrying on successfully a Trade so beneficial t* to the Kingdom

We humbly beg Leave to represent to your Majesty, That we delivered our Opinion very fully the last Year, in our Report on the Weavers Petition, against the wearing of printed, stained, and dyed, Callicoes; and we 'cannot conceive how any Scheme more effectual can be applied, to prevent this Evil, than what was proposed by the Bill depending, the last Sessions, in Parliament; nor hath any thing occurred to us since that time, w hereby we should be induced to alter our Opinion upon this Subject:

However, as the Prohibition thereby intended will be a great Restraint upon the East India Trade, it might be reasonable, that some Advantages should be allowed to the Erast India Company, in lieu thereof, as seems to be proposed by their Lordships Address.

Having the refore discoursed with the Directions of the said Company, we crave Leave to lay before your Majesty an Account of some Privileges and Advantages which the Company are very desirous of; and, having consulted the Commissioners of your Majesty’s Customs upon such of them as relate to their Province, we are of Opinion, that the following Particulars may be granted in favour* of the East India Company, without any Detriment to the Publick, or to your Majesty’s Revenues; but, we presume, whatever new Privileges may be granted th&n, the same will be understood to be in Compensation for the Vol- 19-

Restraint intended to be laid upon the Wearing and Using of printed, stained, and dyed Callicoes

That the Deficiencies on the Funds appropriated to pay the Interest of the Debt due from the Publick to the East India Company may be made good to them, and suitable Provision made to prevent Deficiencies thereon for the future:

That a Law may pass, to put an effectual Stop to any; of your Majesty's Subjects being concerned, for the future, in the Interloping Trade to the East Indies, in Partnership with Foreigners, or in their Service, on any Pretence, or from any Place, whatsoever:

That the Limits of the said Company’s Charter may be extended Five, or Ten, Leagues on this Side the Cape of Good Hope, to prevent the clandestine Trade said to be earned on by hovering Ships that lie off the Dutch Settlements there, and frequently take in Goods at Sea, as well from Dutch as British Ships:

To encourage the Company to make Settlements at Madagascar, by giving them Leave to import such Slaves, as they shall purchase there, directly to the /Vest Indies; provided this Allowance can be so guarded, that np Opportunity may be thereby given to import any other Commodities, purchased in the East Indies, directly to the British Plantations likewise:

To repeal the Law for giving Certificates for foreign Tea imported; whereby great Encouragement is given to the bringing of it from Ustend, and other Places:

To lay severe Penalties on Ships going to St. Helena, or Ascension, to meet Ships there^ if they take in any East India Goods,

To prohibit the Importation of all East India Good* into any of the British Colonies in America, except such as shall be carried thither directly from Great Britain, on the same Penalties and Forfeitures on the Governors, Custom-house Officers, and Importers, as Goods of the Growth, Product, or Manufacture, of Europe, are now prohibited to be imported there from other Places than Great Britain; with proper Encouragement for discovering the Importation:

To lay Penalties on all Ships and Commanders that shall take in any Goods out of any East India Ship, not being within the Limits of the Company’s Charter: Thatifany Goods be unshipped at Sea, or at any other Place, out of a Ship from the East Indies, into any other Ship or Vessel, that then the same, or the Value thereof, shall be forfeited; with a Penalty on the Persons concerned either in unshipping or receiving the said Goods:

That a Rate be put on all unrated East India Goods, provided the same be done in such manner as not to lessen the Produce of the present Funds:

And whereas the Company now stand indebted to the Crown, by Retrospect upon the Duties paid on their Goods, occasioned by a Mistake in the former Manner of computing the said Duties; ap Account of which Retrospect is drawing out by the proper Officers; when the same shall have been laid before your Majesty, and both Houses of Parliament, we shall humbly submit how far it may be reasonable to indulge the Company, in remitting the Money due thereon, or any Part of it:

To allow the Company Five per Cent. prompt Payment, on the Duties arising on the 15per Cent, additional Duty laid on all Goods made of Cotton, and not prohibited, payable on the gross Sale of the Candle, notwithstanding such Goods shall not be sold within the Twelve Months after Importation; it not being the Interest of the Company to prolong the Time of Sale, unless it be for a better Market, wherein the Revenue will find its Account:

To allow the Company, as is allowed to all Other Merchants, 61 per Cent. Discount on the Impost of Custom^ on unrated Goods, although not sold within the Year;* because the Company can sell but twice a Year, an^ other Merchants at any time:

To grant a longer time than a Year for Drawback* on the Company s Goods exported; by which pleans the $ C Goods

A Petition of the Mayor, capital Burgesses, Assistants, clandestine Merchants, Clothiers, Serge-makers, and other Dealers Exportation in the Woollen Manufactures, in the Town and Borough of W°°h of Tiverton, and Places adjacent, in the County of Devon, w’as presented to the House, and read; setting forth, That the said Town and Borough, and Parts adjacent, and many Thousand Families there, chiefly depend on the Woollen Manufacture Trade; which is greatly decayed, by reason of the Exportation of Wool from Ireland to France, upon which no Duty is paid, and by the Running of Wool from England to France; to the utter Ruin of the said Trade, and vast Numbers of Persons whose Livelihoods depend thereon: And praying Relief.

Ordered, That the said Petition do lie upon the Table.

Mr. Kelsall presented to the House, according to Or- South Sea der, a Copy of a Memorial from the South Sea Com- ComPa,v-v* pany, relating to the issuing of Exchequer Bills by way of Loan to the said Company: And also,

The Company’s Obligation for the Million of new Exchequer Bills, and Interest:

And

South Sea Company.

7° Martii.

A. 1720,

And the Titles thereof were read.

The said Copy of the Memorial, and the South Sea Company’s Obligation, are a3 follow; viz.

To the Right honourable the Lords Commissioners of his Majesty’s Treasury.

May it please your Lordships,

THE Court of Directors of the South Sea Company humbly desire, That your Lordships will be pleased, pursuant to an Act of this present Session of Parliament in that behalf, intituled, An Act for making forth new Exchequer Bills, not exceeding One million, at a certain Interest; and for lending the same to the South Sea Company at an higher Interest, upon Security of repaying the same, and such high Interest, into the Exchequer, for Uses to which the Fund for lessening the publick Debts, called the Sinking Fund, is applicable; and for circulating and exchanging, upon Demand, the said Bills, at or near the Exchequer; to issue, or cause to be issued, by way of Loan, or Advance, all the Exchequer Bills, not exceeding One million in principal Money, prepared, or to be prepared, by virtue of the said Act, unto the said Company, or unto Robert Knight Esquire, Cashier of the Company, in Trust for the said Company.

And the said Court of Directors do humbly propose, That the said Company will pay and allow for the principal Sums contained in such Bills, which shall be lent or advanced to the said Company, after the Rate of Four per Cent, per Annum; and that the said Company will repay into the Receipt of his Majesty’s Exchequer the principal Sum so lent, together with Interest, as aforesaid, at the End of One Year from the borrowing thereof; and the said Company are ready to give such Security for Repayment of the same Principal and Interest accordingly, as in and by the said Act is prescribed. Which is humbly submitted.

By Order of the Court of Directors,

South Sea House, D. JVescomb, Secretary.

2 June 1720.

7 th March 1720-1.

Examined by

H. Kelsall

T O all to whom these Presents shall come, the Governor and Company of Merchants of Great Britaifi trading to the South Seas, and other Parts of America; and for encouraging the Fishery; send Greeting: Whereas by an Act of Parliament, of the present, Sixth, Year of his Majesty’s Reign, intituled, An Act for making forth new Exchequer Bills, not exceeding One million, at a certain Interest; and for lending the same to the South Sea Company at ati higher Interest, upon Security of repaying the same, and such high Interest, into the Exchequer, for Uses to which the Fund for lessening the publick Debts, called the Sinking Fund, is applicable; and for circulating and exchanging, upon Demand, the said Bills, at or near the Exchequer; it is Enacted, That the Commissioners of the Treasury, or any Three or more of them, or the High Treasurer, for the Time being, shall have Power to issue, or cause to be issued, by way of Loan, or Advance, all such Bills as should, from time to time, be prepared by virtue of that Act, the Principal contained therein not exceeding One million of Pounds, to the Corporation of the said Governor and Company; the same Corporation, or Body Politick, giving Security upon their then present, and to be increased, Annuity, or yearly Fund, and upon their weekly or other Payments, to be made at the Exchequer, for, or upon account of, their said Annuity, or yearly Fund, for the Repayment of the principal Sum so lent, with an Interest, not exceeding the Rate therein mentioned, for every principal Sum so lent, at such Day or Days, Time or Times, as should be agreed upon by and between the said Commissioners of the Treasury, or any Three or more of them, or the High Treasurer, for the Time being, on behalf of the Publick; and the said Governor and Company of Merchants of Great Britain, or their Court of Directors, on their behalf; so as no such Day or Time should be more remote than the First Day of

March One thousand Seven hundred Twenty-one, or the End of the then next Session of Parliament: And the said Commissioners of the Treasury, and High Treasurer, for the Time being, are thereby directed and required to take especial care, that, upon Repayment of the principal Monies so to beJent, the same, with the Interest or Increase accruing thereupon, be received, and be applied, in the First Place, to the paying off and discharging the said newr Exchequer Bills to be made forth in pursuance of that Act; and that the Surplus thereof, after paying off and discharging the same new Exchequer Bills, shall be placed at the said Receipt of Exchequer, to and for the same Uses, Intents, and Purposes, to which the Monies of the Surplusses, Excesses, and Over-plusses, commonly called the Sinking Fund, are applicable: And that the said Governor and Company of Merchants of Great Britain shall make just Account of the principal Money so borrowed, and of the said Interest and Increase thereof, and of the Repayment of the same Principal, with the said Interest or Increase thereof, into the Exchequer, in manner as aforesaid; and, in Default of repaying the said Monies so to be lent, with the said Interest or Increase thereof, at the Day or Days, Time or Times, to be limited for that Purpose, as aforesaid, then the said Commissioners of the Treasury, or any Three or more of them, or the High Treasurer, for the Time being, shall cause the Money so lent to be stopped out of the Monies which weekly, or otherwise, shall be payable to the said Corporation, at the Exchequer, for or upon the then present, or to be increased, Annuity, or yearly Fund, of the same Corporation, together with so much more as the Interest of the Money, so unpaid, shall then amount unto; and to cause the Principal and Interest, so stopped, to be applied and placed in the Exchequer, as aforesaid, as by the said Act of Parliament may more fully appear: And whereas the Court of Directors of the said Corporation have desired the Commissioners of his Majesty’s Treasury, pursuant to the said Act, to issue, or cause to be issued, by way of Loan, or Advance, all the Exchequer Bills, not exceeding One million in principal Money, prepared, or to be prepared, by virtue of the said Act, unto the said Company, or to the Cashier thereof for the said Company; and the said Court of Directors have proposed, That the said Company will pay and allow for the principal Sums contained in such Bills, which shall be lent or advanced to the said Company, Interest after the Rate of Four Pounds per Centum per Annum; and that the said Company will repay, into the Receipt of his Majesty’s Exchequer, the principal Sum so lent, together with Interest, as aforesaid, at the End of One Year from the borrowing thereof; which Proposal the Commissioners of his Majesty’s Treasury have judged to be reasonable, and have agreed thereunto on behalf of the Publick: Now know ye, That the said Governor and Company of Merchants of Great Britain, for themselves, and their Successors, do, by these Presents, under their Common Seal, covenant, promise, and grant, to and with our Sovereign Lord George, by the Grace of God, of Great Britain, France and Ireland, King, Defender of the Faith, S;c. his Heirs and Successors, That they the said Governor and Company of Merchants of Great Britain, or their Successors, shall and will well and truly repay, or cause to be repaid, in good and lawful Money of Great Britain, into the Exchequer at Westminster, all and every such Sum and Sums as shall be issued to them in Exchequer Bills, by way of Loan, or Advance, pursuant to the said Act, as aforesaid; together with Interest for the same, after the said Rate of Four Pounds per Cent, per. Annum; and that all and every such Sum and Sums, so to be repaid, with such Interest thereof, shall be paid and satisfied at the End of One Year, to be reckoned from the Time, or respective Times, of issuing the said Bills by w ay of Loan, or Advance, as aforesaid, without brawl, or further Delay: And that they the said Governor and Company of Merchants of Great Britain, and their Successors, shall and w ill make jurt Account of the principal Mon es so borrowed, and of the Interest and Increase

thereof,

thereof, and of the Repayment of the same Principal, with the said Interest or Increase thereof, into the Exchequer, in such manner as by the said Act is required: And for the better securing the Repayment of the Sum and Sums to be borrowed by the said Governor and Company, as aforesaid, with Interest, at the End of One Year, according to the true Meaning of the said Act, and of these Presents, they, the said Governor and Company of Merchants of Great Britain, for themselves, and their Successors, do hereby declare, grant, and agree, that their present, and to be increased, Annuity, or yearly Fund, and their weekly and other Payments, to be made at the Exchequer, for or upon Account of their said Annuity, or yearly Fund, are, and shall be, a Security, and are, and shall be, subject and liable to and for the Repayment of the principal Sums so to be borrowed by them, with the said Interest, after the said Rate of Four Pounds per Cent.per Annum, at the End of One Year, to be reckoned as aforesaid, according to the Tenor and true Meaning of the said Act, and of their Covenant herein before contained, in that behalf: And if Default shall be made of repaying the said Sum and Sums to be lent, with the said Interest or Increase thereof, or any Part of the same, at the End of One Year, to be reckoned next after the Time, or respective Times of borrowing the same, as aforesaid; together with so much more as the Interest of the Money so unpaid shall then amount unto; and to apply the same Principal and Interest to and for the Purposes in the said Act prescribed, in such Manner and Form as are thereby directed and intended. In Witness whereof, the said Governor and Company have caused their Common Seal to be affixed to these Presents, dated the Fourth Day of June in the Year of our Lord One thousand Seven hundred land Twenty; and in the Sixth Year of his said Majesty’s Reign.

To the honourable the Knights, Citizens, and Burgesses, in Parliament assembled; pursuant to an Order from this honourable House, the following Copy is humbly presented:

AFTER our hearty Commendations: Whereas by an Act, lately passed in Parliament, intituled, An Act for making forth Exchequer Bills, not exceeding One million, at a certain Interest; and for lending the same to 6 D the

the South Sea Company, at an higher Interest upon Security of repaying the same, and* such high Interest, into the Exchequer, for Uses to which the Fund for lessening the publick Debts, called the Sinking Fund, is applicable; and for circulating and exchanging, upon Demand, the said Bills at or near the Exchequer; we are, amongst other Things, impowered, at any time or times, within One Year from the Tenth Day of May 1720, and from thence to the End of the then next Session of Parliament, and by such Proportions at a time as we shall find to be most for the Advantage of the Publick, to make forth, or cause to be made forth, at the Exchequer, in such Method and Form as we shall think most convenient, any Number of new Exchequer Bills, not exceeding One million of Pounds Sterling; and the said Bills are to bear an Interest not exceeding Two Pence per Cent, per Diem, and to be Current in all publick Payments; and to be circulated and exchanged by Trustees to be appointed for that Purpose; as in and by the said Act, relation being the reunto had, may more fully appear: These are, in pursuance of the Power to us given by the said Act of Parliament, and for the more regular safe making and issuing the said Bills, from time to time, that the following Rules, Orders, and Instructions, be observed by you, and every of you, herein concerned; that is to say, That you, the Auditor of the Receipt, do cause indented Bills to be made forth, according to the Form hereby approved, and herewith sent you, not exceeding the Sum of One million, bearing an Interest after the Rate of One Pcny per Cent, per Diem; and that you sign the said Bills, and cause them to be numbered, and also sealed or marked with a Portcullis; and that you cause Books to be made of the Cheques, Indents, or Counterfoils from which the said Exchequer Bills shall be cut, as well for trying the Truth thereof, as for keeping an Account of the Sums issued thereby; one Part of which said Books are to be kept in your Office, and the other Part to be delivered to the said Trustees; which they are to re-deliver when the said Bills, are to be cancelled: And you, the said Auditor, are to deliver over the Bills, which shall he made forth, from time to time, by virtue of the said Act, to the Four Tellers of his Majesty's Exchequer, to be placed as so much Cash in their respective Offices; which Bills are intended to be lent to the South Sea Company, upon such Security as we shall approve, and such Warrant as we shall make in that behalf: And you are to keep an exact Account, in the nature of a Comptrol, whereby you.are to charge the said Tellers, respectively* with the Monies which shall be contained in the Bills sq by you delivered to them: And you are to give in Charge to the said Tellers, That they do also cause to be kept a true Account of all the Bills, which they shall so receive from you; and of their issuing, receiving back, and delivering out, the same: And yourself, and the said Tellers, are strictly injoined and required, in all Matters and Things, touching the said Bilk, to observe the Prescriptions and Directions of the said Act of Parliament; and such further Rules and Methods as we, or the High -Treasurer, or Commissioners of the Treasury, for the Time being, shall find necessary for his Majesty’s Service: And, for so doing, this shall be your Warrant.

Whitehall, Treasury Chambers, 28th April 1720.
